observations:
Torah #227 is an exceptionally brief teaching (3 sentences, reported in the name of an unnamed tzaddik). Its entire conceptual content is captured by the two packages already proposed:

- Package 1 (evil): רְשָׁעִים / עֲשָׂבִים עַל הַגַּגּוֹת / חָצִיר גַּגּוֹת
- Package 2 (good): תְּבוּאָה הַנִּקְצֶרֶת / בִּרְכַּת ה' / עֲלִיָּה

The teaching has no sub-themes, no intermediate domains, no letters or archetypal figures, and no eitza chains complex enough to suggest an independent thematic cluster.

The only candidate for a third package would be קְצִירָה (harvesting itself) as a neutral structural concept — the mechanism that separates the two poles. However, קְצִירָה is not given independent bechina language in the text; it functions solely as a contextual activity (the passersby say the blessing WHILE the harvesting is happening), not as a standalone concept equated with other things via 'זֶה בְּחִינַת'. For this reason, it does not meet the threshold (3+ concepts connected by explicit bechina language forming an independent domain) required for a new package.

Conclusion: The two proposed packages (evil mirror + good mirror) fully account for the entire conceptual content of Torah #227. The teaching is structured as a single binary contrast, not as a multi-stage argument with multiple independent domains.
